Office and Principle Room users (192.168.3.x, 192.168.4.x)
report they cannot reach Server Room (1.0.0.x) or Internet Lab
(128.168.0.x). IT Department and CS Department users say the
same. But Server Room ↔ Internet Lab works fine internally.
Find the broken link.

injection.action: shut down the WAN link to router1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 Serial2/0 (eth2), 20.20.0.0/8 link
Mechanism: router1 ↔ router2 over the 20.20.0.0/8 serial is
  the only path connecting routers 0/1's subnets to router2's
  Server Room + Internet Lab. With the link down, RIP on both
  sides ages out the unreachable prefixes and connectivity
  splits into two islands (router0+router1 side / router2 side).
Localization: router2 eth2 (or router1 eth3)
Root cause: WAN link router1<->router2 (20.20.0.0/8) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth2 up` on router2
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth2 up` on router2

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: The WAN inter-router link between Router1 and Router2 (wan_r1_r2). The failure is specifically on Router2’s eth2 interface.

Mechanism: All campus user VLANs (IT 192.168.1.0/24, CS 192.168.2.0/24, Office 192.168.3.0/24, Principle 192.168.4.0/24) reach Server Room (1.0.0.0/8) and Internet Lab (128.168.0.0/16) via Router1 toward Router2. Router1 has RIP-learned routes to 1.0.0.0/8 and 128.168.0.0/16 via next hop 20.20.0.2 (Router2), but the link to that next hop is down, so traffic cannot cross from campus to those networks. Server Room and Internet Lab still communicate internally on Router2, so they appear fine to each other.

Localization: Router2 eth2 (wan_r1_r2) is down. Evidence:
- Router2 ip addr shows eth2 state DOWN with 20.20.0.2/8 configured and no LOWER_UP; ifconfig flags lack UP/RUNNING.
- Ping from Router2 to 20.20.0.1 (Router1) fails with “Network is unreachable.”
- Ping from Router1 to 20.20.0.2 (Router2) is 100% loss.
- Router1’s eth3 (20.20.0.1/8) is UP.

Root cause: Router2’s WAN interface eth2 on the r1–r2 link is administratively/physically down, breaking connectivity.

Corrective fix: On router2, bring up the interface: ip link set dev eth2 up (verify 20.20.0.2/8 is set). Then confirm L1/L2 (carrier/link light) and rerun pings between 20.20.0.1 and 20.20.0.2. Ensure RIP/zebra are running so routes propagate; if needed, restart routing daemons. After restoration, campus users should reach 1.0.0.0/8 and 128.168.0.0/16.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies the router1<->router2 WAN link (20.20.0.0/8) as down and pins the failure to Router2's eth2 interface (20.20.0.2).
The report explicitly states the WAN link down isolates Router2’s networks from the campus (Server Room/Internet Lab still talk to each other while campus VLANs cannot), i.e. two islands.
Corrective fix explicitly instructs bringing up Router2 eth2 (ip link set dev eth2 up) and verifying connectivity/routing, which matches the expected remediation.

The log contains concrete test results (router1->20.20.0.2: 100% loss; router2->20.20.0.1: 'Network is unreachable') that reasonably indicate the r1–r2 WAN is down and justify the split-islands diagnosis, but the investigator asserted specific interface state details (eth2/eth3 UP/DOWN and exact IP bindings) that are not shown in the captured ifconfig outputs and they did not fetch routes or daemon state to fully eliminate alternative causes.
